title: A written duration is built at run time, not stored as a constant.
text: `rule:types/duration` folds `30s` to one nanosecond count while compiling, and `lower::Lowering::lower_duration` then emits an `InstKind::CoreCall` to `nvs_types::CORE_DURATION_FROM_NANOS` on that count, so every evaluation builds a fresh `Core\Time\Duration` object. The remaining half is emitting the value into the compiled unit's constant pool as an immortal object, so `{timeout: 30s}` allocates nothing at run time. That is a latency question on the request path, not a semantic one: the value is identical either way.
